slides: In the last question we used factorials. Factorials come up on the exam quite often, also as pure math, with no story at all.

slides.say: So let's learn the tools, one at a time, with examples.
First, the factorials to know by heart. One factorial is one, two factorial is two, and three factorial is six.
at: the factorials to know by heart

slides.say: Four factorial is twenty-four. Five factorial is five times twenty-four, a hundred twenty.
Each one is the one before, times the next number. Six factorial is six times a hundred twenty, seven hundred twenty.
And seven factorial is seven times seven hundred twenty, five thousand forty.
One more fact. Zero factorial is one, by definition. It comes up rarely, but now you know it.
Why know them by sight? Because the exam hides them. Now a new example. a factorial is twelve times ten. What is a?
at: a factorial is twelve times ten

slides.say: Twelve times ten is a hundred twenty, and a hundred twenty is five factorial. So a is five.
One more. b factorial is eight times ninety. Eight times ninety is seven hundred twenty, and that's six factorial. So b is six.
at: b factorial is eight times ninety
Eight times ninety is seven hundred twenty

slides.say: The second tool is the one from the last question. We expand a factorial only as far as we need.
Eight factorial is eight times seven factorial. Or, if we need it, eight times seven times six factorial.
at: Eight factorial is eight times seven factorial
eight times seven times six factorial

slides.say: For example, ten factorial over eight factorial. Ten factorial is ten times nine times eight factorial. Eight factorial cancels, on top and below. We get ten times nine, ninety.
The same works with letters. n plus one, factorial, is n plus one, times n factorial.
Let's see it in numbers. Four factorial is four times three factorial. Twenty-four is four times six.
at: Four factorial is four times three factorial

slides.say: So a factorial over the factorial just before it is the bigger number. Twelve factorial over eleven factorial is twelve.
And n factorial over n minus one, factorial, is n.
at: n factorial over n minus one

slides.say: Now the third tool. A big factorial over a smaller one. For example, seven factorial over four factorial.
Seven factorial is seven times six times five times four factorial. Four factorial cancels, on top and below.
at: Seven factorial is seven times six

slides.say: What's left is seven times six times five. Seven times six is forty-two. Then forty-two times five is two hundred ten.
So b factorial over a factorial is always a run of neighbours. That means whole numbers in a row, from a plus one up to b.
Now backwards, a type the exam likes. b factorial over a factorial is thirty, and b is bigger than a. What are a and b?
at: b factorial over a factorial is thirty

slides.say: We need neighbours that multiply to thirty. Five times six is thirty.
The run ends at b, so b is six.
The run starts right after a, at five. So a is four, not five. Careful, that's the common slip.
at: The run starts right after a

slides.say: Let's check. Six factorial over four factorial is six times five, thirty.
One more. b factorial over a factorial is ninety. Nine times ten is ninety. So b is ten, and a is eight.
at: b factorial over a factorial is ninety

slides: The exam usually limits the numbers, for example to below ten. That way only one run of neighbours fits. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
